spec_notes: docs/shiploop/spec.md does not contradict the request. It marks three choices as its own ("Default of 2026-11-22"): repeated names collapse to one member, amounts must be safe integers, and one process owns each data file. It decides without marking that a member list with any empty or invalid entry is rejected (R-2 "Missing or invalid names"), that a fresh file starts with no groups, and that invalid share values (negative, fractional) get 400. It never says that balances sum to 0, what fields a settlement has ({from,to,cents}), or that settlements bring every balance to 0. Those are only implied by the algorithm. It pins "an equal split of 100 among three members assigns 34, 33 and 33", which any correct build shares. It also pins that a refused expense uses no index and that 404 comes before body validation, which a correct build need not share.
tests_notes: TC-1 bundles group validation, 409, empty balances and settlements, and 404 on four routes. TC-3 bundles about 20 invalid bodies plus numbering. In TC-3 the zero and negative cents cases are sent with exact shares {Bo:10}, which the share check rejects anyway, so removing the positive-amount check goes unnoticed (proved for S-22). Tied to this build: every test waits for the stdout line "Listening on port N", and TC-8 tests symlink handling. Would fail on another correct build of the request: TC-1 expects ["Ada","Bo","Ada"] to be accepted (rejecting duplicates is also acceptable) and ["Ada","Bo",""] to be refused (ignoring the empty entry is defensible). TC-3 expects cents "10" to be refused (coercion is acceptable per U-3). TC-7 expects 1.0000000000000001 to be refused. TC-9 expects "." and ".." to be refused and "..." to be accepted. TC-6 expects __proto__ and constructor as member names and ids.
maintainer: The concurrency guarantee rests on recordExpense and createGroup running validation, saveState and the reply with no await in between, so the in-memory state is never stale. Adding any asynchronous step there (for example an async file write) would quietly break S-34, and only TC-5 would notice. The JSON.parse reviver that relies on the source-text context argument, and the hand-built JSON strings for BigInt balances and settlements, are unusual and easy to break when edited.
